outcomes.text: Study one modern-world period study and one wider-world depth study, each a coherent narrative of change.
Apply causation, consequence, change and interpretations to modern-world history.
Explain the geography of North America, the Great American Desert and Manifest Destiny.
Explain why settlers went west and the challenges they faced: Mormons, pioneer farmers, miners.
Describe the Plains Indians' way of life and early US government policy towards them.
Explain increasing conflict on the Plains: Fort Laramie, the Indian Wars, Sand Creek and Fetterman's Trap.
Explain the background to the Civil War: North-South differences, slavery, abolitionism, Lincoln and Davis, and its impact on civilians.
Describe coming to terms with the Mormons and the Mountain Meadow Massacre.
Explain the aftermath of the Civil War: amendments, Civil Rights Act, Reconstruction and federal-state powers.
Describe the settlement of the west: Homesteaders, government laws, railroads and farming.
Explain the resolution of the 'Indian problem': reservations, Little Big Horn, Dawes Act, Wounded Knee and the closing frontier.

subtopics.title: Germany and the growth of democracy

outcomes.text: Explain the difficulties of ruling Germany under Kaiser Wilhelm: parliament, militarism, industry and socialism.
Explain the impact of the First World War: defeat, end of the monarchy, reparations, the Ruhr and hyperinflation.
Explain Weimar democracy: early unrest, the Stresemann recovery, international agreements and culture.
Explain the impact of the Depression on support for the Nazis and Hitler's appeal.
Explain the failure of Weimar democracy and Hitler becoming Chancellor.
Explain how Hitler built a dictatorship: the Reichstag Fire, Enabling Act, Night of the Long Knives and Führer.
Describe economic changes under the Nazis and the impact of war on Germans.
Explain Nazi social policy and its impact on women, youth, churches, racial persecution and the Final Solution.
Explain Nazi control: propaganda, censorship, the police state, and opposition and resistance.
Describe Russia's economy and society before 1914.
Explain Nicholas II's autocracy, the 1905 Revolution, the Dumas and Stolypin's policies.
Explain how the First World War and Rasputin led to the Tsar's abdication.
Explain the failure of the Provisional Government and the Bolshevik October Revolution.
Explain Lenin's dictatorship, the Cheka, the Civil War and Bolshevik success.
Explain War Communism, Kronstadt and the New Economic Policy.
Explain how Stalin gained and used power: Purges, terror, censorship and the cult of personality.
Explain collectivisation, the Five Year Plans and their consequences.
Describe the impact of the Second World War on the USSR.
Explain the 1920s Boom: consumer society, mass production and inequality of wealth.
Describe social and cultural developments: cinema, jazz and the position of women.
Explain the divided society: crime, prohibition, racial tension, the Klan and the Red Scare.

subtopics.title: Bust: the Depression and New Deal

outcomes.text: Describe American society in the Depression and Hoover's response.
Judge the effectiveness of the New Deal for different groups, and opposition to it.
Explain the impact of the Second World War on the US economy and society.
Describe post-war prosperity, the American Dream, McCarthyism and popular culture.
Explain racial tension and the Civil Rights campaigns of the 1950s and 1960s.
Explain the Great Society and the feminist movements of the 1960s and 1970s.

topics.title: BA Conflict and tension: the First World War, 1894-1918

subtopics.title: Causes of the First World War

outcomes.text: Explain the alliance system and the Morocco and Balkan crises.
Explain Anglo-German rivalry: Weltpolitik, colonies and the naval race.
Explain the outbreak of war: Sarajevo, the July Crisis and the Schlieffen Plan.
Explain the Schlieffen Plan, its failure and the Battle of the Marne.
Describe Western Front tactics, technology and the battles of Verdun, the Somme and Passchendaele.
Describe the wider war: Gallipoli, Jutland and the U-boat campaign.
Explain the effect of Russia's withdrawal and America's entry on the war.
Explain the 1918 military developments leading to Germany's defeat.
Explain Germany's surrender: the blockade, the Kaiser's abdication and the armistice.

topics.title: BB Conflict and tension: the inter-war years, 1918-1939

outcomes.text: Explain the peacemakers' aims and the Fourteen Points.
Describe the Versailles Settlement: territory, military limits, war guilt and reparations.
Evaluate the treaty and wider settlement, including reactions and problems of new states.
Describe the League's formation, organisation, powers and agencies.
Judge the League's successes and failures in the 1920s.
Explain diplomacy outside the League: Locarno and the Kellogg-Briand Pact.
Explain the League's collapse: the Depression, Manchuria and Abyssinia.

subtopics.title: Origins of the Second World War

outcomes.text: Explain the development of tension: Hitler's aims, German rearmament and the Stresa Front.
Explain escalation: the Rhineland, Axis, Anschluss, appeasement and Munich.
Explain the outbreak of war: Czechoslovakia, the Nazi-Soviet Pact, Poland and responsibility.

topics.title: BC Conflict and tension between East and West, 1945-1972

outcomes.text: Explain the end of the Second World War: Yalta, Potsdam and US-Soviet ideologies.
Explain the Iron Curtain, the Truman Doctrine, the Marshall Plan and the Berlin Blockade.
Explain events in Asia: Communist China, Korea and Vietnam.
Describe military rivalries: the arms race, NATO, the Warsaw Pact and the space race.
Explain the Thaw: Hungary and the U2 Crisis.
Explain the building of the Berlin Wall.
Explain tensions over Cuba: the Bay of Pigs and the missile crisis.
Explain the Prague Spring and the Brezhnev Doctrine.
Explain the easing of tension, Détente and SALT 1.

topics.title: BD Conflict and tension in Asia, 1950-1975

outcomes.text: Explain the causes of the Korean War.
Describe the development of the war: Inchon, Chinese intervention and MacArthur's sacking.
Explain the end of the war and its impact.
Explain the end of French rule and civil war in South Vietnam.
Explain US involvement: the Domino Theory and Strategic Hamlets.
Explain Johnson's War: Tonkin, bombing, protests, My Lai and the Tet Offensive.
Explain Nixon's War: Vietnamisation, bombing and widening into Laos and Cambodia.
Explain opposition to the war, including Kent State and the media.
Explain the end of the war: Paris talks, US withdrawal and the fall of Saigon.

topics.title: BE Conflict and tension in the Gulf and Afghanistan, 1990-2009

outcomes.text: Explain regional instability: the Iran-Iraq war, oil and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
Explain the 1990 Gulf War: Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, UN action and consequences.
Explain Al-Qaeda's aims, bin Laden and the 11 September attacks.
Describe Afghanistan under the Taliban and attitudes to it.
Explain Bush's war on terror and the overthrow of the Taliban.
Describe Saddam Hussein's regime and international attitudes to it.
Explain the 2003 invasion: WMD, oil, the military campaign and opposition.
Explain the war's impact: insurgency, elections, terrorism and the 2007 surge.
Study one British thematic study over three eras, plus one British depth study with its historic environment.
Apply similarity, difference, change, continuity and significance to British history.

topics.title: AA Britain: Health and the people: c1000 to the present day

outcomes.text: Describe medieval medicine: natural and supernatural ideas, Hippocratic and Galenic methods, and doctors.
Explain medical progress: Christianity, hospitals, Islamic medicine and surgery.
Explain medieval public health and the Black Death.
Explain the impact of the Renaissance: Vesalius, Paré and Harvey, and opposition to change.
Describe dealing with disease: treatments, quackery, hospitals and John Hunter.
Explain prevention: inoculation and Jenner's vaccination.
Explain Germ Theory and the work of Pasteur, Koch and Ehrlich.
Explain the revolution in surgery: anaesthetics, antiseptics and asepsis.
Explain improvements in public health: cholera, reformers and the Public Health Acts.
Describe modern treatment of disease: pharmaceuticals, penicillin and antibiotic resistance.
Explain how war and technology changed surgery.
Explain modern public health: Booth and Rowntree, Liberal reforms, Beveridge and the NHS.

topics.title: BB Britain: Power and the people: c1170 to the present day

outcomes.text: Explain constraints on kingship and Magna Carta.
Explain the origins of Parliament and Simon de Montfort.
Explain the Peasants' Revolt and royal authority.
Explain the Pilgrimage of Grace and the royal response.
Explain Divine Right, the English Revolution and the Commonwealth.
Explain the causes and significance of the American Revolution.
Explain the extension of the franchise: the Great Reform Act and Chartism.
Explain protest and change: anti-slavery, Anti-Corn Law League and factory reformers.
Explain the growth of trade unions.
Explain the campaign for women's suffrage and progress to equality.
Explain workers' rights: the General Strike and union reform.
Explain minority rights, discrimination and the Brixton Riots.

topics.title: AC Britain: Migration, empires and the people: c790 to the present day

outcomes.text: Explain Viking and Anglo-Saxon invasion, the Danelaw and Cnut's North Sea Empire.
Explain the Norman Kingdom and Angevin Empire.
Explain the Hundred Years' War and the birth of English identity.
Explain sugar, the Caribbean and the slave trade.
Explain British colonisation of North America and the War of Independence.
Describe migrants to and from Britain: Huguenots, Highland clearances and Ulster plantations.
Explain British expansion in India.
Explain British expansion in Africa and the Boer War.
Describe migration to, from and within Britain in the Empire era.
Explain the end of Empire and independence movements.
Explain the legacy of Empire: Windrush, Asian and African migration.
Explain Britain's relationship with Europe.
Explain the causes of the Norman Conquest.
Describe the military aspects: Stamford Bridge, Hastings, tactics and castles.
Explain how the Normans established and maintained control.
Explain feudalism, government and the Domesday Book.
Describe economic and social changes under the Normans.
Explain Lanfranc's reform of the Church and Church-state relations.
Describe monasticism, learning and education.

subtopics.title: The historic environment of Norman England

outcomes.text: Analyse a specified Norman site in its historical context.

topics.title: BB Medieval England - the reign of Edward I, 1272-1307

subtopics.title: Government, the rights of King and people

outcomes.text: Explain Henry III's legacy and Edward I's character.
Explain the development of government, rights and justice.
Describe trade, towns and villages and royal finance.
Describe education and learning.
Describe the development of the legal system.
Describe medieval warfare, tactics and technology.
Explain the invasion and colonisation of Wales.
Explain relations with Scotland and Wallace.

subtopics.title: The historic environment of Medieval England

outcomes.text: Analyse a specified medieval site in its historical context.
Describe Elizabeth I, her court and ministers.
Explain the difficulties of a female ruler: Parliament, marriage and Essex's rebellion.
Describe the Golden Age: prosperity, fashion and theatre.
Explain poverty and responses to it.
Describe English sailors: Hawkins, Drake and Raleigh.
Explain religious matters: Catholics, Puritans and Elizabeth's policies.
Explain the challenge of Mary Queen of Scots.
Explain the conflict with Spain and the Armada.

subtopics.title: The historic environment of Elizabethan England

outcomes.text: Analyse a specified Elizabethan site in its historical context.

subtopics.title: Crown, Parliament, plots and court life

outcomes.text: Explain Crown and Parliament after the Restoration.
Explain the Catholic question, plots and the Exclusion Bill.
Describe Charles II's court.
Explain the Great Plague and the Fire of London.
Describe Restoration culture, science and architecture.
Describe overseas land and the East India Company.
Explain trade, the Navigation Acts and the slave trade.
Describe naval warfare and the Dutch Wars.

subtopics.title: The historic environment of Restoration England

outcomes.text: Analyse a specified Restoration site in its historical context.
